events.label: central bank: Federal Reserve raises rates
events.headline: US Federal Reserve raises interest rates to fight persistent inflation
events.summary: The US Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate for the first time in three years to fight high inflation and the effects of rising gas prices. This decision creates pressure on other central banks, like India's Reserve Bank, as they consider their own upcoming rate choices amid currency pressures.

articles.title: Federal Reserve hikes key rate to tackle ‘too high’ inflation, defying Trump demands for cut
articles.snippet: Chairperson Warsh said renewed U.S.-Iran combat, which has driven up gas prices, also convinced officials to support rate hikes; President Trump reacted angrily to the decision, renewing his call for the Fed to lower interest rates “AND FAST”

articles.title: US Federal Reserve raises rates after 3 years: Is RBI rate hike coming? October MPC meet in focus
articles.snippet: The US Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike complicates the Reserve Bank of India's future decisions. While some analysts predict rate increases in October and December, others anticipate the RBI will maintain its current stance amid inflation and currency pressures.

articles.title: ‘Fed’ up with inflation? US rate hike leaves RBI with an October-or-December dilemma, economists say
articles.snippet: The US Federal Reserve’s first rate hike since 2023 has added to pressure on India, with the rupee breaching 96 against the dollar and economists increasingly debating when the RBI could follow with a hike of its own. Emkay sees an October move as increasingly likely, while HDFC Bank expects the central bank could wait until December as it weighs inflation, growth, energy prices and currency pressures.

events.label: central bank: Bank of England seen holding rates
events.headline: Bank of England holds interest rates steady amid rising inflation
events.summary: The Bank of England kept its benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75 percent as inflation rose to 3.1 percent. This matters because growing price pressures from energy costs could lead to tighter monetary policies and future rate hikes.

articles.title: Bank of England sounds inflation alarm as it holds interest rates
articles.snippet: The Bank of England has decided to hold interest rates steady at 3.75 percent and is currently halting gilt sales. With inflation risks escalating, there are concerns prices may exceed four percent next year. Governor Andrew Bailey indicated that ongoing conflict might require a shift towards tighter monetary measures. Interestingly, three members of the Monetary Policy Committee pushed for a rate hike.

articles.title: Bank of England defies Fed’s rate-hike lead, leaving rates unchanged
articles.snippet: The Bank of England kept rates steady Thursday, even after U.K. inflation rose to 3.1% and energy costs put pressure on prices.

articles.title: Global Market: Bank of England seen holding rates as UK inflation climbs
articles.snippet: The Bank of England is expected to hold its 3.75% benchmark rate for a sixth meeting despite UK inflation rising to 3.1% in August. Higher fuel and energy costs linked to the Iran conflict are intensifying price pressures. Policymakers will monitor wages and domestic inflation, while markets anticipate possible rate hikes later.

articles.title: UK inflation jumps to 3.1% as energy costs soar
articles.snippet: The reading comes a day before the Bank of England updates its monetary policy.
